collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A visitor claims a villager's fish trap design as their own: confront them publicly, or quietly prove whose it is.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) invented a new fish trap that catches twice as much. A visitor who saw it last season has been telling other islands that (other.he/she) invented it. (friend) heard it from a trader. (subject) is hurt and angry. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: When the visitor next comes, (subject) asks (other.him/her), in front of everyone, to explain how the trap works. The visitor gets it wrong. The village laughs. The visitor leaves red-faced, and the traders start calling it (subject)'s trap.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) builds an even better trap and sends it to the other islands with a trader, as a gift, with (subject.his/her) mark carved on it. Before long, everyone knows whose trap it is. (subject) never says a word against the visitor.
